subtopics.title: National income, growth and base years
subtopics.concept: National income measures how much a country produces in a year. The main measures are GDP, GNP and NNP, and each one adds or subtracts one item from the last. subtopics.notes:
### The national income family
GDP counts what is produced **inside India**, by anyone. Other measures start from GDP and change one item at a time.

| Measure | How to get it |
|---|---|
| GDP | Final goods and services made within India in a year |
| GNP | GDP + NFIA |
| NNP | GNP - depreciation |
| National income | NNP at factor cost |
| Per capita income | National income / population |

NFIA means net factor income from abroad. It is what Indians earn abroad minus what foreigners earn here. Depreciation is the wear and tear of machines.

> **Example:** GDP is ₹100 and NFIA is ₹5. So GNP is ₹105.

The chain to remember is GDP, then GNP, then NNP, then national income. NNP at factor cost is the textbook meaning of "national income".

### Factor cost and market price
Market price is what buyers pay. Factor cost is what producers earn.

> **Rule:** Market price = factor cost + indirect taxes - subsidies.

Indirect taxes raise the price. Subsidies hold it down. If factor cost is ₹900, taxes are ₹120 and subsidies are ₹20, market price is ₹1000.

### Nominal and real GDP
Nominal GDP uses this year's prices. It can rise only because prices rose. Real GDP uses the prices of a fixed base year. It shows real production.

The link between them is the GDP deflator.

$$\text{Deflator} = \frac{\text{Nominal GDP}}{\text{Real GDP}} \times 100$$

Nominal GDP ₹330 and real GDP ₹300 give a deflator of 110. Prices are 10% above the base year.

> **Tip:** To get real GDP, divide nominal GDP by (deflator / 100).

### Three ways to measure
All three methods aim at the same total.

- **Income method:** add wages, rent, interest and profit.
- **Expenditure method:** add consumption, investment, government spending and net exports, written $C + I + G + (X-M)$.
- **Product method:** add the value added at each stage, so nothing is counted twice.

India now reports sectors as Gross Value Added (GVA) at basic prices. GDP equals GVA plus product taxes minus product subsidies. Estimates come in stages: advance, provisional, revised and final.

### Three sectors and core industries
| Sector | Examples |
|---|---|
| Primary | Agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining |
| Secondary | Manufacturing, construction, electricity |
| Tertiary (services) | Trade, transport, finance, IT, public administration |

India is a services-led economy. Services give over half of GVA.

The **eight core industries** are coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement and electricity. They carry a large weight in the IIP.

### Base years and who publishes
The **NSO** (National Statistical Office) works under **MoSPI**. It was formed in 2019 by merging the CSO and NSSO. The Economic Survey is different. The Department of Economic Affairs in the Finance Ministry issues it, a day before the Budget.

| Indicator | Old base | New base |
|---|---|---|
| GDP | 2011-12 | 2022-23 (27 Feb 2026) |
| CPI | 2012 | 2024 (12 Feb 2026) |
| IIP | 2011-12 | 2022-23 (from 1 Jun 2026) |
| WPI | 2011-12 | 2022-23 (15 Jun 2026) |

> **Watch:** GDP and IIP use a financial-year base. CPI uses a calendar year, 2024.

subtopics.title: Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog
subtopics.concept: India ran twelve Five Year Plans from 1951 to 2017. The Planning Commission made them. On 1 January 2015 NITI Aayog replaced the Commission. NITI is a think tank and does not allocate plan funds.

tricks.title: Plan story line
tricks.body: Farm (1st), machines (2nd), wars (3rd), holiday, stability (4th), Garibi Hatao (5th), rolling plan, reforms (8th), inclusive (11th), sustainable (12th), then NITI.

example.q: Which plan coincided with the LPG reforms?
steps: The reforms began in 1991.
The plans after the annual plans of 1990-92 began in 1992.
That is the 1992-97 plan.

tricks.title: Two gaps
tricks.body: Plan Holiday was 1966-69. Annual Plans were 1990-92.

example.q: Why was there a 'Plan Holiday'?
steps: The 1962 and 1965 wars hit the economy.
Drought made it worse.
The 3rd plan was derailed and annual plans ran in 1966-69.
example.answer: War and drought derailed the 3rd Plan.

mistakes.right: It was set up by a Cabinet resolution.

mistakes.right: Harrod-Domar is the 1st Plan. Mahalanobis is the 2nd.

mistakes.wrong: Saying NITI Aayog allocates plan funds.
mistakes.right: It advises and monitors. It does not allocate funds.

mistakes.right: Holiday means annual plans after the 3rd plan. Rolling means revised every year.

subtopics.notes:
### From plans to NITI
The **Planning Commission** was set up on 15 March 1950 by a **Cabinet resolution**. The Prime Minister was its chairman. It steered twelve Five Year Plans from 1951 to 2017.

From 1 January 2015 a Cabinet resolution created **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India). Neither body is constitutional or statutory.

### The plans and their ideas
| Plan | Period | Idea |
|---|---|---|
| 1st | 1951-56 | Harrod-Domar model; agriculture and irrigation |
| 2nd | 1956-61 | Mahalanobis model; heavy industry |
| 3rd | 1961-66 | Self-reliance; Gadgil strategy; broken by wars and drought |
| Plan Holiday | 1966-69 | Three annual plans |
| 4th | 1969-74 | Growth with stability |
| 5th | from 1974 | Garibi Hatao; ended early |
| Rolling plan | 1978-80 | Lakdawala concept |
| 6th | 1980-85 | Poverty removal; IRDP and NREP begin |
| 7th | 1985-90 | Food, work, productivity |
| Annual plans | 1990-92 | Transition years |
| 8th | 1992-97 | Started with the 1991 LPG reforms |
| 9th | 1997-2002 | Growth with social justice |
| 10th | 2002-07 | 8% growth target |
| 11th | 2007-12 | Faster and more inclusive growth |
| 12th | 2012-17 | Faster, more inclusive, sustainable growth |

> **Tip:** The 2nd plan is Mahalanobis, and Mahalanobis means machines.

### Breaks in the plan sequence
Two gaps and one special idea are asked often.

- **Plan Holiday (1966-69):** the 1962 and 1965 wars and drought derailed the 3rd plan. Three annual plans followed.
- **Rolling plan (1978-80):** the plan is revised every year. D.T. Lakdawala is linked to the concept.
- **Annual plans (1990-92):** they ran before the delayed 8th plan.

The 12th plan was the last. It ran to 2017, and then NITI took over.

### NITI Aayog: who is in it
The **Prime Minister chairs** NITI Aayog. The **Governing Council** has all Chief Ministers and the Lt Governors of Union Territories. The PM appoints a Vice-Chairperson and full-time members. A **CEO** runs the daily work.

Its ideas are **cooperative federalism**, where states are partners, and **competitive federalism**, where states are ranked.

### What NITI produces
NITI does not make Five Year Plans. It writes three documents:

1. a **15-year vision**
2. a **7-year strategy**
3. a **3-year action agenda**

Its well-known products are the SDG India Index, the state Multidimensional Poverty Index, the Composite Water Management Index and the Aspirational Districts Programme (2018, 112 districts).

### Planning Commission versus NITI
| Point | Planning Commission | NITI Aayog |
|---|---|---|
| Started | 15 March 1950 | 1 January 2015 |
| Origin | Cabinet resolution | Cabinet resolution |
| Role | Made plans, allocated funds | Advises, monitors, builds indices |

> **Watch:** NITI is not statutory and does not allocate plan funds.

subtopics.title: Money, banking and the RBI
subtopics.concept: The RBI is India's central bank. It issues currency, keeps the banks' reserves and sets the policy rates. A six-member Monetary Policy Committee decides the repo rate to keep CPI inflation at 4%, with a band of 2% either side. Most questions test dates, rate positions and the ratios CRR and SLR.

tricks.title: Corridor arithmetic
tricks.body: Repo is the middle. The floor (SDF) is repo minus 0.25. The ceiling (MSF and Bank Rate) is repo plus 0.25.

example.q: If repo were 6.00%, what would the MSF be?
steps: MSF is the ceiling.
Ceiling = repo + 0.25.

tricks.title: Nationalisation anchors
tricks.body: 1935 RBI born, 1949 RBI nationalised, 1955 SBI, 1969 fourteen banks, 1975 RRBs, 1980 six banks.

example.q: How many banks were nationalised in 1980?
steps: The 1969 round had 14 banks.
The 1980 round was smaller.
It covered banks with deposits of ₹200 crore or more.

tricks.title: MPC fixed points
tricks.body: Six members. At least four meetings a year. Target CPI 4% with a 2% band. The Governor has the casting vote.

example.q: Who has the casting vote in the MPC?
steps: The MPC has an even number of members.
A tie needs a tie-breaker.
The RBI Governor holds it.

mistakes.wrong: Repeating old rates such as repo 6.5% and CRR 4%.
mistakes.right: After the 5 Aug 2026 MPC, repo is 5.25% and CRR is 3%.

mistakes.wrong: Mixing up reverse repo (3.35%, dormant) and SDF (5.00%).
mistakes.right: SDF is the operative floor of the corridor.

mistakes.wrong: Crediting the Nachiket Mor Committee with the 1990s reforms.
mistakes.right: Those were Narasimham I and II. Nachiket Mor (2014) is about inclusion and payment banks.

mistakes.wrong: Calling CRR and SLR 'policy rates'.
mistakes.right: They are ratios. The policy rate is the repo rate.

mistakes.wrong: Saying the RBI issues the ₹1 note.
mistakes.right: The Finance Ministry issues the ₹1 note and coins.

subtopics.notes:
### The RBI in brief
The RBI Act, 1934 created the bank. It began work on **1 April 1935**. It was **nationalised on 1 January 1949**. Its head office is in **Mumbai**.

The RBI issues all currency except the **₹1 note and coins**. The Finance Ministry issues those. The RBI is also banker to the government and banker to banks. It is the **lender of last resort**. It keeps the country's forex reserves.

The Governor is **Sanjay Malhotra**, the 26th Governor, since December 2024.

### The rate corridor
The **repo rate** is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term to banks. It is the main policy rate. Two rates sit around it.

| Rate | Position | Level (after 5 Aug 2026 MPC) |
|---|---|---|
| MSF and Bank Rate | Repo + 0.25 (ceiling) | 5.50% |
| Repo | Middle | 5.25% |
| SDF | Repo - 0.25 (floor) | 5.00% |

The MPC held rates unchanged in August 2026 with a neutral stance. The reverse repo is 3.35%, but it is dormant as an operative rate since the SDF began in 2022.

> **Rule:** SDF is the floor and MSF is the ceiling. Bank Rate equals MSF.

SDF lets banks park spare cash with the RBI without collateral. MSF lets banks borrow overnight, even beyond their SLR holdings.

### CRR, SLR and liquidity
- **CRR:** the share of deposits a bank keeps as **cash with the RBI**. It earns no interest. It is now **3.00%**, cut from 4% in four steps in Sep-Nov 2025.
- **SLR:** the share of deposits a bank keeps in liquid assets such as government securities and gold, held by the bank itself. It is **18%**.
- **OMOs:** the RBI buys or sells government securities. Buying adds liquidity.

> **Tip:** Cutting CRR or repo makes money cheaper and adds liquidity. Raising them controls inflation.

### The Monetary Policy Committee
The RBI (Amendment) Act, 2016 set up the MPC. It has **six members**: three from the RBI, including the Governor, and three named by the government. The Governor has the **casting vote**.

It meets at least four times a year. The target is **CPI inflation of 4% with a 2% band on each side**. Missing the band for three straight quarters means a report to the government. The target uses CPI, not WPI.

### Money supply
| Measure | Contents |
|---|---|
| M1 (narrow money) | Currency with the public + demand deposits + other RBI deposits |
| M2 | M1 + post-office savings |
| M3 (broad money) | M1 + time deposits |
| M4 | M3 + post-office deposits (not NSCs) |

### Banking milestones
| Year | Event |
|---|---|
| 1955 | SBI formed from the Imperial Bank |
| 1969 | 14 banks nationalised (19 July) |
| 1975 | Regional Rural Banks begin |
| 1980 | 6 more banks nationalised (15 April) |
| 1991, 1998 | Narasimham Committees I and II |
| 2008 | NPCI set up (UPI came in 2016) |
| 2014 | Nachiket Mor Committee |

DICGC insures deposits up to **₹5 lakh** per depositor per bank. Payment banks take deposits but cannot lend.

The Governor has the casting vote.

Three straight quarters outside the band trigger a report.

example.q: Who holds the casting vote in the Monetary Policy Committee?

The Governor breaks the tie.

patterns.name: CRR, SLR and liquidity tools
patterns.howToSpot: 'CRR is kept with', 'SLR consists of', or 'which tool adds liquidity at once'.
steps: CRR means cash with the RBI. It earns nothing.
SLR means the bank's own liquid assets.
A CRR or repo cut adds liquidity. A rise removes it.

example.q: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) requires banks to keep what?
steps: CRR is a share of deposits.
It is held as cash.
The cash sits with the RBI and earns no interest.
example.answer: A fixed share of their deposits as cash with the RBI

patterns.name: Money supply and banking milestones
patterns.howToSpot: 'M1 consists of', 'which is the broad money measure', '14 banks were nationalised in', or DICGC and NPCI facts.
steps: M1 = currency + demand deposits + other RBI deposits.
M3 = M1 + time deposits.
Recall DICGC ₹5 lakh and NPCI 2008.
patterns.why: Each measure adds one item to the last.

example.q: Which item is included in M1 but not in M3?
steps: M3 is M1 plus time deposits.
So every M1 item is also in M3.
The correct answer is that there is no such item.

subtopics.title: Inflation and price indices
subtopics.concept: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level. It comes from higher demand or higher costs. CPI measures retail prices and the RBI targets it. WPI measures wholesale goods and is compiled by the Office of Economic Adviser.

tricks.title: Compiler pairs
tricks.body: CPI, IIP and GDP come from MoSPI (NSO). WPI and PPI come from DPIIT's Office of Economic Adviser.

example.q: Who compiles the WPI?
steps: WPI covers wholesale goods.
It is a commerce-side index.
The Office of Economic Adviser in DPIIT compiles it.

tricks.title: Core is headline without the volatile part
tricks.body: Core inflation = headline minus food and fuel. Stagflation = stagnation plus inflation.

example.q: Headline CPI is 6%. Food and fuel contribute 2.5%. What is core?
steps: Core = headline - food and fuel part.

mistakes.wrong: Using WPI for the inflation target.
mistakes.right: The MPC targets CPI.

mistakes.wrong: Giving WPI the old 2011-12 base.
mistakes.right: Since 15 June 2026 WPI uses 2022-23 with 957 items.

mistakes.wrong: Calling disinflation 'deflation'.
mistakes.right: Disinflation is a slower rise. Deflation is a fall.

mistakes.wrong: Saying WPI includes services.
mistakes.right: WPI covers goods only. CPI includes services.

mistakes.wrong: Treating IIP as a price index.
mistakes.right: IIP measures industrial output.

subtopics.notes:
### Types of inflation
Inflation means prices keep rising. The same ₹100 buys less over time.

| Type | Cause or meaning |
|---|---|
| Demand-pull | Too much demand chasing goods (cheap credit, tax cuts) |
| Cost-push | Costlier inputs such as oil, fertiliser, wages |
| Stagflation | High inflation with stagnant growth |
| Disinflation | Inflation still positive but slowing |
| Deflation | Prices falling |
| Hyperinflation | Runaway triple-digit monthly rise |

> **Tip:** Ask one question. Did demand rise, or did costs rise?

### Headline and core
**Headline inflation** covers all items. **Core inflation** is headline minus food and fuel. Core shows the steadier, underlying trend.

Food has the largest weight in the CPI basket. A monsoon shock moves headline sharply while core stays steadier.

### The main price indices
| Index | Agency | Base |
|---|---|---|
| CPI (Combined) | NSO, MoSPI | 2024 (new series Feb 2026); old 2012 |
| WPI | Office of Economic Adviser, DPIIT | 2022-23 (Jun 2026); old 2011-12 |
| CPI-IW | Labour Bureau | Used for dearness allowance |
| CPI-AL, CPI-RL | Labour Bureau | Farm and rural labourers |
| IIP | NSO | 2022-23 from 1 Jun 2026; old 2011-12 |

IIP measures industrial output, not prices.

### CPI versus WPI
- **CPI** measures retail prices. It includes services.
- **WPI** measures wholesale or producer prices. It covers goods only. It has no services.

The 2026 WPI revision raised the basket from **697 to 957 items**. It also introduced Producer Price Indices (PPI).

> **Watch:** The RBI targets CPI, not WPI. The target is 4% with a 2% band.

### Inflation targeting
The RBI Act was amended in **2016**. The MPC now aims at **CPI inflation of 4% plus or minus 2%**. The RBI has failed if inflation stays outside the band for **three consecutive quarters**.

### Small facts
- CPI-IW drives dearness allowance for central employees.
- The food part of CPI is called CFPI.
- WPI fuel and power and manufactured products are the volatile groups.
- The Eight Core Industries index feeds the IIP. The eight are coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement and electricity.
- The GDP deflator is nominal GDP divided by real GDP, times 100.

patterns.name: Identify the inflation type
patterns.howToSpot: A story about an oil shock, monsoon failure or credit boom. The type is asked.
steps: Ask: did demand rise or did costs rise?
Higher demand (cheap loans, tax cuts) is demand-pull.
Costlier inputs (crude, wages) is cost-push.
Falling prices is deflation. Slower inflation is disinflation.
patterns.why: The cause in the story gives the label.

example.q: A sharp rise in imported crude oil prices pushes up general prices. What is this?
steps: Crude oil is an input.
Input cost rose.
Demand did not need to rise.

patterns.name: Index, agency and coverage
patterns.howToSpot: 'The WPI is compiled by', 'which index does the RBI target', or 'which index covers services'.
steps: CPI (Combined) comes from NSO, MoSPI.
WPI comes from the Office of Economic Adviser, DPIIT.
CPI-IW, CPI-AL and CPI-RL come from the Labour Bureau.
WPI is goods only. CPI includes services.
patterns.why: Each index has one agency and one coverage.

example.q: The Wholesale Price Index in India is released by which office?
steps: WPI is a commerce-ministry series.
It sits in DPIIT.
The Office of Economic Adviser releases it.
example.answer: Office of Economic Adviser, DPIIT (not the NSO)

patterns.name: Base years and new series
patterns.howToSpot: 'The new CPI series uses which base year', 'the WPI basket was expanded to', or 'the IIP base'.
steps: New CPI base is 2024 (February 2026).
New WPI and IIP base is 2022-23.
WPI items went from 697 to 957.
Old bases were 2012 (CPI) and 2011-12 (WPI, IIP).
patterns.why: Match each index to its new year.

example.q: The new Consumer Price Index series released in February 2026 has which base year?
steps: CPI uses a calendar year.
It replaced the 2012 base.
The new year is 2024.

patterns.name: Core versus headline
patterns.howToSpot: 'Core inflation excludes', 'headline inflation means', or a statement on food and fuel.
steps: Headline is the full published index.
Core = headline minus food and fuel.
Food has a big CPI weight, so headline jumps with supply shocks.
Disinflation is slower inflation. Deflation is negative.
patterns.why: Core removes the volatile items.

example.q: Core inflation is best described as what?
steps: Start with headline inflation.
Remove food and fuel.
What remains is the underlying trend.
example.answer: Headline inflation excluding food and fuel

patterns.name: CPI variants, IIP and core industries
patterns.howToSpot: 'DA is linked to which CPI', 'IIP measures', or 'the eight core industries include'.
steps: CPI-IW from the Labour Bureau drives dearness allowance.
CPI-AL and CPI-RL track farm and rural labourers.
IIP measures output, not prices.
Learn the eight core industries as one list.
patterns.why: These small facts are fixed and easy to match.

example.q: Which index is used to revise the dearness allowance of central employees?
steps: Dearness allowance follows industrial workers' prices.
That is CPI-IW.
The Labour Bureau compiles it.
example.answer: CPI-IW (Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers)

revision: Demand-pull is excess demand. Cost-push is costlier inputs.
Stagflation is inflation with stagnation. Core = headline - food and fuel.
CPI: retail, includes services, NSO (MoSPI), base 2024.
WPI: wholesale, goods only, DPIIT, base 2022-23, 957 items.
CPI-IW, CPI-AL and CPI-RL come from the Labour Bureau.
The RBI targets CPI at 4% with a 2% band.
IIP is output, re-based to 2022-23.

subtopics.title: Budget and fiscal policy
subtopics.concept: The Budget is the government's yearly plan of income and spending. The Constitution calls it the Annual Financial Statement (Article 112). The main test topics are the four deficits, the three funds and the Budget dates. Budget 2026-27 put the fiscal deficit at 4.3% of GDP.

tricks.title: Number sheet 2026-27
tricks.body: Spend 53.5, receipts 36.5, borrowing 16.9 (₹ lakh crore). Fiscal deficit 4.3%, revenue deficit 1.5%, primary deficit 0.7%. Capex 12.2. Debt 55.6%.

example.q: What is the fiscal deficit in Budget 2026-27?
steps: Recall the deficit trio: 4.3, 1.5, 0.7.
Fiscal deficit is the largest of the three.
It equals ₹16.96 lakh crore of borrowing.

tricks.title: Article trio for money
tricks.body: 112 is the Budget. 266 is the Consolidated Fund and Public Account. 267 is the Contingency Fund.

example.q: Which article covers the Annual Financial Statement?
steps: The Budget is the Annual Financial Statement.
Recall the trio 112, 266, 267.
The first one is the Budget.

mistakes.wrong: Quoting 4.4% as the 2026-27 fiscal deficit.
mistakes.right: 4.4% is the 2025-26 revised estimate. The 2026-27 budget estimate is 4.3%.

mistakes.wrong: Confusing primary deficit with revenue deficit.
mistakes.right: Primary = fiscal deficit - interest. Revenue = revenue expenditure - revenue receipts.

mistakes.wrong: Thinking the Railway Budget is still separate.
mistakes.right: It merged with the Union Budget in 2017.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Article 112 defines the word 'Budget'.
mistakes.right: Article 112 uses the term Annual Financial Statement.

mistakes.wrong: Saying the Contingency Fund is at Parliament's disposal.
mistakes.right: It is at the President's disposal (Article 267).

subtopics.notes:
### The Budget and the Constitution
The word "Budget" is not in the Constitution. **Article 112** calls it the **Annual Financial Statement**. Article 265 says no tax can be levied without the authority of law.

Since **2017** the Budget is presented on **1 February**. The Railway Budget was merged into it in the same year. The **Economic Survey** comes a day before, from the Department of Economic Affairs.

Spending goes through **Demands for Grants** and the **Appropriation Bill**. Taxes go through the **Finance Bill**.

### The three funds
| Fund | Article | Key point |
|---|---|---|
| Consolidated Fund | 266(1) | All revenues and loans; Parliament must approve each withdrawal |
| Public Account | 266(2) | Money held in trust (provident funds, small savings); no vote needed |
| Contingency Fund | 267 | At the President's disposal for unforeseen spending; corpus ₹30,000 crore (2021) |

### Revenue and capital
- **Revenue receipts:** taxes, interest, dividends.
- **Capital receipts:** borrowings, disinvestment, loan recoveries.
- **Revenue expenditure:** salaries, subsidies, interest.
- **Capital expenditure:** roads, buildings, defence equipment.

### The deficits
> **Rule:** Fiscal deficit = total expenditure - total receipts excluding borrowings.

| Deficit | Formula |
|---|---|
| Revenue | Revenue expenditure - revenue receipts |
| Effective revenue | Revenue deficit - grants for capital assets |
| Fiscal | Total expenditure - receipts excluding borrowings |
| Primary | Fiscal deficit - interest payments |

The fiscal deficit is the year's total borrowing need. The primary deficit removes interest on past debt. Interest payments are the largest expenditure head. Subsidies and defence follow.

> **Example:** Expenditure ₹45 lakh crore, receipts without borrowing ₹39 lakh crore. The fiscal deficit is ₹6 lakh crore.

### FRBM Act
The **FRBM Act, 2003** sets legal limits on deficits. It was amended in 2018 to add debt targets. Budgets announce a fiscal **glide path**, a year-by-year route for the deficit as a share of GDP.

### Budget 2026-27 at a glance
Nirmala Sitharaman presented it on 1 February 2026. These are budget estimates.

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Total expenditure | ₹53.47 lakh crore |
| Receipts (excluding borrowings) | ₹36.52 lakh crore |
| Borrowings | ₹16.96 lakh crore |
| Fiscal deficit | 4.3% of GDP (RE 2025-26: 4.4%) |
| Revenue deficit | 1.5% of GDP |
| Primary deficit | 0.7% of GDP |
| Capital expenditure | ₹12.2 lakh crore |
| Central debt | 55.6% of GDP |
| Disinvestment target | ₹80,000 crore |

New in the Budget: Biopharma SHAKTI (₹10,000 crore), SME Growth Fund (₹10,000 crore), Semiconductor Mission 2.0 and MAT cut from 15% to 14%.

patterns.name: Deficit arithmetic
patterns.howToSpot: Expenditure, receipts and interest figures are given. One deficit is asked.
steps: Write the formula for the deficit asked.
Fiscal = total expenditure - receipts excluding borrowings.
Primary = fiscal deficit - interest payments.
Check the units (lakh crore).
patterns.why: One subtraction gives the answer once the formula is right.

example.q: Total expenditure is ₹45 lakh crore. Receipts excluding borrowings are ₹39 lakh crore. What is the fiscal deficit?
steps: Fiscal deficit = expenditure - receipts excluding borrowings.

patterns.name: Budget structure, articles and funds
patterns.howToSpot: 'Which article is the Annual Financial Statement', 'the Contingency Fund is at whose disposal', or a fund-and-article match.
steps: 112 is the Annual Financial Statement.
266(1) is the Consolidated Fund. 266(2) is the Public Account.
267 is the Contingency Fund, at the President's disposal.
Only the Consolidated Fund needs Parliament's vote for withdrawals.
patterns.why: Each fund has one article and one rule.

example.q: The Contingency Fund of India is placed at whose disposal?
steps: It is for unforeseen spending.
Article 267 sets it up.
The President controls it.

patterns.name: Revenue versus capital, effective revenue deficit
patterns.howToSpot: 'Which is a capital receipt', 'effective revenue deficit excludes', or a list with disinvestment, borrowings and grants.
steps: Capital receipts: borrowings, disinvestment, loan recoveries.
Capital expenditure builds assets: roads, buildings, defence equipment.
Revenue expenditure: salaries, subsidies, interest.
ERD = revenue deficit - grants for capital assets.
patterns.why: Sort each item as revenue or capital by asking if it creates a liability or an asset.

example.q: Which of these is a capital receipt?
steps: Borrowings and loan recoveries are capital receipts.
Selling government shares also counts.
That sale is called disinvestment.

patterns.name: FRBM and the glide path
patterns.howToSpot: 'The FRBM Act was passed in', 'a glide path means', or a statement on deficit targets.
steps: FRBM Act is 2003.
A 2018 amendment added debt targets.
A glide path is a year-by-year deficit route.
Interest is the largest expenditure head.
patterns.why: The Act and the glide path are fixed facts.

example.q: In which year was the FRBM Act enacted?
steps: FRBM stands for Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management.
It set legal deficit limits.
It dates from 2003.

patterns.name: Budget process, dates and documents
patterns.howToSpot: 'Since which year is the Budget on 1 February', 'the Economic Survey is tabled when', or Demands for Grants questions.
steps: From 2017 the Budget is on 1 February.
The Railway Budget merged the same year.
The Economic Survey comes a day before, from the DEA.
Spending goes through the Appropriation Bill. Taxes go through the Finance Bill.
patterns.why: The dates and the two bills are fixed.

example.q: When is the Economic Survey presented?
steps: It reviews the economy.
The Department of Economic Affairs prepares it.
It comes a day before the Budget.
example.answer: A day before the Union Budget

revision: Budget = Annual Financial Statement (Article 112). Presented 1 February since 2017.
Railway Budget merged in 2017. Economic Survey comes a day before.
Funds: Consolidated 266(1), Public Account 266(2), Contingency 267.
Contingency Fund is with the President; corpus ₹30,000 crore.
RD = revenue exp - revenue receipts. FD = total exp - receipts excluding borrowings. PD = FD - interest.
ERD = revenue deficit - grants for capital assets.
FRBM Act 2003, amended 2018. Interest is the largest expenditure head.

subtopics.title: Taxation and GST
subtopics.concept: A direct tax falls on the person who pays it, like income tax. An indirect tax is passed on to buyers, like GST. GST began on 1 July 2017, and GST 2.0 cut it to two main slabs, 5% and 18%, from 22 September 2025. The new Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026.

tricks.title: GST article trio
tricks.body: 246A is the power to tax. 269A is inter-state GST. 279A is the Council. All came from the 101st Amendment, in force from 1 July 2017.

example.q: Which article created the GST Council?
steps: Recall the trio 246A, 269A, 279A.
The last one is the Council.
The 101st Amendment (2016) inserted it.

tricks.title: GST 2.0 slab story
tricks.body: Two working slabs: 5 (merit) and 18 (standard). 40 is kept for sin and luxury goods. 12% and 28% ended on 22 September 2025.

example.q: What is the GST on a small car now?
steps: Small cars were at 28% plus cess.
The 28% slab was abolished.
Small cars moved to the standard slab.

tricks.title: Tax-year switch
tricks.body: Income-tax Act, 2025 works from 1 April 2026. One 'tax year' replaces the previous year and assessment year pair. 536 sections, 23 chapters.

example.q: From which income year does the term 'Tax Year' apply?
steps: The Act started on 1 April 2026.
That is the start of FY 2026-27.
So that year is Tax Year 2026-27.

mistakes.wrong: Calling STT an indirect tax.
mistakes.right: STT is a direct tax on securities transactions.

mistakes.wrong: Thinking compensation cess still applies to all goods.
mistakes.right: It ended on 22 September 2025, except on pan masala and tobacco products.

mistakes.wrong: Saying the GST Council decides by a simple majority.
mistakes.right: It needs a three-fourths weighted majority. Centre has 1/3 of votes, states 2/3.

mistakes.wrong: Still listing a 12% or 28% GST slab.
mistakes.right: GST 2.0 kept 5% and 18%, plus a 40% demerit rate.

mistakes.wrong: Using IGST for a sale inside one state.
mistakes.right: Inside one state it is CGST + SGST. IGST is for inter-state sales and imports.

mistakes.wrong: Saying the Centre taxes agricultural income.
mistakes.right: Agricultural income is outside income tax. Taxing it is a state power.

subtopics.notes:
### Direct and indirect taxes
A direct tax is borne by the person who pays it. An indirect tax is paid to the government but passed on to buyers through prices.

| Type | Examples | Can the burden shift? |
|---|---|---|
| Direct | Income tax, corporate tax, capital gains tax, STT | No |
| Indirect | GST, customs duty, excise on petroleum and alcohol, stamp duty | Yes, to the consumer |

STT is the securities transaction tax. It is a direct tax.

Direct taxes are progressive: a higher income pays a higher rate. Indirect taxes are regressive, because rich and poor pay the same rate on a good. But they are easy to collect.

> **Example:** A shop adds GST to your bill. The shop pays it to the government, but you bear it. So GST is an indirect tax.

Corporation tax and personal income tax are the two biggest direct taxes. GST is the biggest indirect tax. **Agricultural income** is outside income tax, because taxing it is a state power.

### GST basics
GST (Goods and Services Tax) is one tax on goods and services. The **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016** created it. It began on **1 July 2017**.

It is a **destination-based consumption tax**. The tax follows the place where the goods are consumed. GST took over excise, service tax, VAT, CST, entry tax and luxury tax.

| Article | What it covers |
|---|---|
| 246A | Power to make GST laws |
| 269A | GST on inter-state trade (IGST) and its sharing |
| 279A | The GST Council |

### Which GST applies
- A sale **within one state** carries CGST (to the Centre) plus SGST (to the state).
- A sale **between states**, and imports, carry **IGST**.
- The **GSTN** is the IT network that runs GST.

> **Example:** A ₹1,000 item taxed at 18% is sold within one state. CGST is ₹90 and SGST is ₹90. Total tax is ₹180.

### The GST Council
The **Union Finance Minister** chairs the Council. The other members are the Union Minister of State for Finance and the state finance ministers. The quorum is half the members.

Decisions need a **three-fourths weighted majority**. The Centre holds **one-third** of the votes. All states together hold **two-thirds**.

> **Rule:** Neither side can pass a decision alone. One-third and two-thirds are both below three-fourths.

### GST 2.0, the 2025 slab reform
The 56th Council meeting approved it on 3 September 2025. It took effect on **22 September 2025**.

| Slab | Used for |
|---|---|
| 5% | Merit goods |
| 18% | Standard rate |
| 40% | Demerit goods: tobacco, pan masala, some luxury items |

The **12% and 28% slabs were abolished**. Small cars, ACs and TVs moved to 18%. Unprocessed food, education and health stay exempt. Compensation cess ended, except on pan masala and tobacco products. Compensation to states under the GST law ran from July 2017 to June 2022.

### The new Income-tax Act
The **Income-tax Act, 2025** was passed in August 2025. It replaced the 1961 Act from **1 April 2026**. It has 536 sections in 23 chapters, in plainer language.

Its key change is one **tax year**. It replaces the old pair "previous year" and "assessment year". So income of FY 2026-27 is called Tax Year 2026-27.

Filing is still yearly. The default **new regime** has lower rates but few deductions. The older regime stays as an option. Under the new regime (Budget FY 2025-26), income up to ₹12 lakh pays no tax. For salaried people, the limit is ₹12.75 lakh with the standard deduction.

### Other tax facts
- **LTCG** (long-term capital gains) on equities is taxed at 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh, since Budget 2024.
- STT was raised in Budget 2026.
- Share buybacks are taxed as capital gains for holders. Promoters also face a buyback tax.
- The **Finance Commission** (Article 280) decides how central taxes are shared with states.
- Cesses and surcharges are outside the shared pool, so states get no part of them.

patterns.name: GST Council and constitutional articles
patterns.howToSpot: 'Article 279A deals with', 'who chairs the GST Council', or 'the Centre has what share of votes'.
steps: Recall the articles: 246A power, 269A inter-state, 279A Council.
The Union Finance Minister chairs the Council.
Members add the Union MoS Finance and state finance ministers.
Decisions need 3/4 of weighted votes: Centre 1/3, states 2/3.
patterns.why: Three articles and one voting rule cover almost every Council question.

example.q: Under which article of the Constitution is the GST Council constituted?
steps: The 101st Amendment added three articles.
246A and 269A deal with taxing power and inter-state trade.
279A sets up the Council.

patterns.name: GST launch and the 2025 slab reform
patterns.howToSpot: 'GST was introduced from', 'which amendment brought GST', or 'the GST slabs after September 2025 are'.
steps: GST began on 1 July 2017.
The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 created it.
GST 2.0 took effect on 22 September 2025.
Slabs are now 5% and 18%, plus 40% for demerit goods.
patterns.why: The launch date and the new slabs are fixed, often-asked facts.

example.q: After the GST 2.0 reform of 22 September 2025, what are the two main GST slabs?
steps: The 12% and 28% slabs were abolished.
5% is for merit goods. 18% is the standard rate.
40% is only for demerit goods.

patterns.name: Direct versus indirect tax
patterns.howToSpot: 'Which is a direct tax', 'which tax cannot be shifted', or options mixing customs, corporate tax, GST and STT.
steps: Ask: can the payer pass the tax on to a buyer?
If not, it is direct: income, corporate, STT, capital gains.
If yes, it is indirect: GST, customs, excise, stamp duty.
STT is the usual trick option. It is direct.
patterns.why: The burden test sorts every option in one pass.

example.q: Which of the following is a direct tax? (a) GST (b) Customs duty (c) Corporate tax (d) Stamp duty
steps: GST, customs and stamp duty are passed on to buyers.
Corporate tax falls on company profits.
The company cannot shift it.

patterns.name: Income-tax Act 2025 and the tax year
patterns.howToSpot: 'The new Income-tax Act is effective from', 'the tax year replaces', or 'how many sections does the new Act have'.
steps: The Act was passed in August 2025.
It works from 1 April 2026 and replaces the 1961 Act.
One 'tax year' replaces previous year and assessment year.
It has 536 sections in 23 chapters.
patterns.why: A new law is a favourite current-affairs question.

example.q: From which date did the Income-tax Act, 2025 come into force?
steps: It replaced the Income-tax Act, 1961.
It starts with a financial year.
That year began on 1 April 2026.

patterns.name: Tax bases, exemption and devolution
patterns.howToSpot: 'Agricultural income is taxed by', 'which tax gives the most direct-tax revenue', or 'how are taxes shared with states'.
steps: Agricultural income is outside income tax. It is a state subject.
Corporation tax and personal income tax lead direct taxes. GST leads indirect taxes.
The Finance Commission (Article 280) shares central taxes with states.
Cesses and surcharges are outside the shared pool.
patterns.why: These are fixed statements that show up in true/false options.

example.q: Which statement about agricultural income in India is correct?
steps: Income tax is a central tax.
Taxing agricultural income is a state power.
So the Income-tax Act leaves it out.
example.answer: It is outside central income tax; only states can tax it

patterns.name: Which GST applies to a sale
patterns.howToSpot: 'A sale from one state to another attracts', 'GST on imports is', or 'CGST and SGST are levied on'.
steps: Check if buyer and seller are in the same state.
Same state: CGST (Centre) + SGST (state).
Different states, or an import: IGST.
The GSTN only runs the IT system. It is not a tax.
patterns.why: The place of sale alone decides the GST type.

example.q: A trader in Gujarat sells goods to a buyer in Rajasthan. Which GST applies?
steps: Seller and buyer are in different states.
This is an inter-state sale.
Inter-state sales carry IGST.

patterns.name: Taxes merged into GST
patterns.howToSpot: 'Which tax was not subsumed in GST', 'GST replaced which taxes', or 'which tax is still outside GST'.
steps: GST took over excise, service tax, VAT, CST, entry tax and luxury tax.
Customs duty is still outside GST.
Excise on petroleum and alcohol continues.
Pick the option that is still levied separately.
patterns.why: Learn the merged list once and the odd one out is clear.

example.q: Which of these taxes was NOT merged into GST? (a) Service tax (b) VAT (c) Customs duty (d) Entry tax
steps: Service tax, VAT and entry tax were merged.
Customs is charged on imports at the border.
It is still a separate tax.

revision: Direct: income, corporate, STT, capital gains. Indirect: GST, customs, excise (petroleum, alcohol), stamp duty.
GST: 101st Amendment (2016), from 1 July 2017. Articles 246A, 269A, 279A.
GST Council: Union FM chairs; 3/4 weighted majority; Centre 1/3, states 2/3.
CGST + SGST inside a state. IGST between states and on imports. GSTN is the IT network.
GST 2.0 from 22 September 2025: 5% and 18%, plus 40% demerit. 12% and 28% abolished.
Income-tax Act, 2025 from 1 April 2026: one 'tax year'; 536 sections, 23 chapters.
New regime: no tax up to ₹12 lakh (₹12.75 lakh for salaried).
Agricultural income is not taxed by the Centre. Tax sharing goes through the Finance Commission (Article 280).

subtopics.title: Government schemes and missions
subtopics.concept: A scheme question tests four hooks: launch year, ministry, benefit and purpose. Learn each flagship scheme as one line with its number, such as ₹6,000 for PM-KISAN or ₹5 lakh for PM-JAY. The big recent change is VB-G RAM G, which replaced MGNREGA from 1 July 2026 with 125 days of work.

tricks.title: Launch-year clusters
tricks.body: 2014: Jan Dhan, Make in India, Swachh Bharat. 2015: BBBP, APY, MUDRA, PMAY. 2016: Ujjwala, Startup India. 2018: Ayushman. 2019: PM-KISAN. 2020: SVANidhi, PLI. 2023: Vishwakarma, Drone Didi. 2024: Surya Ghar. 2026: VB-G RAM G.

example.q: Which scheme gives ₹6,000 a year to farmers?
steps: ₹6,000 is the PM-KISAN number.
It started in 2019.
The Agriculture Ministry runs it.

tricks.title: MGNREGA to RAM G swap
tricks.body: 100 days became 125. Wages every 15 days became weekly. Act of 2025, in force from 1 July 2026.

example.q: From when does VB-G RAM G apply?
steps: It was passed as an Act in 2025.
It replaced MGNREGA.
It came into force in mid-2026.

tricks.title: MUDRA ladder
tricks.body: Shishu up to ₹50,000. Kishor ₹50,000-5 lakh. Tarun ₹5-10 lakh. Tarun Plus up to ₹20 lakh. The names go from child to young adult.

example.q: A MUDRA loan of ₹3 lakh falls in which tier?
steps: Shishu ends at ₹50,000.
Kishor covers ₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh.
₹3 lakh lies in that range.

mistakes.wrong: Naming one ministry for Beti Bachao Beti Padhao.
mistakes.right: BBBP is a joint scheme of three ministries.

mistakes.wrong: Stopping MUDRA at ₹10 lakh.
mistakes.right: Tarun Plus goes up to ₹20 lakh since October 2024.

mistakes.wrong: Saying MGNREGA still gives 100 days.
mistakes.right: VB-G RAM G replaced it from 1 July 2026, with 125 days.

mistakes.wrong: Mixing up PMSBY and PMJJBY.
mistakes.right: PMSBY is accident cover (₹20 a year). PMJJBY is life cover.

mistakes.wrong: Giving PM-JAY cover per person.
mistakes.right: PM-JAY gives ₹5 lakh per family a year.

mistakes.wrong: Putting Jal Jeevan Mission under Swachh Bharat.
mistakes.right: JJM (2019) is tap water. SBM (2014) is sanitation.

subtopics.notes:
### How to read a scheme question
Every scheme question asks one of four things: **launch year, ministry, benefit or purpose**. Learn one line per scheme. News brings new schemes each month, but these flagships appear in every paper.

> **Tip:** Match the number first. ₹6,000 a year means PM-KISAN. ₹5 lakh health cover means PM-JAY. 125 days means VB-G RAM G.

### Jobs and livelihoods
- **MGNREGA** (Act 2005, working from 2006): 100 days of wage work a year per rural household.
- **VB-G RAM G** replaced MGNREGA from **1 July 2026**, under a 2025 Act. The full name is Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin). The guarantee rose to **125 days**. Wages are paid weekly, not every 15 days.
- **DAY-NRLM** (2011): rural livelihoods through women's self-help groups (SHGs). **DAY-NULM** (2014) is the urban twin. Both sit under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana.
- **PM SVANidhi** (2020): working-capital loans for street vendors.
- **PM Vishwakarma** (2023): support for 18 traditional trades.
- **Namo Drone Didi** (2023) gives drones to women SHGs. **Lakhpati Didi** (2023) aims at ₹1 lakh+ yearly income for them.

### Bank accounts, loans and insurance
| Scheme | Launch | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| PM Jan Dhan Yojana | 28 Aug 2014 | Zero-balance accounts, RuPay card, overdraft |
| MUDRA Yojana | 8 Apr 2015 | Loans without collateral |
| Atal Pension Yojana | 2015 | Pension for unorganised workers aged 18-40 |
| Sukanya Samriddhi | 2015 | Savings for the girl child |
| PMSBY | - | Accident cover of ₹2 lakh for ₹20 a year |
| PMJJBY | - | Life insurance cover |

Jan Dhan is the world's largest financial-inclusion drive. PMSBY and PMJJBY are the two Jan Suraksha insurance schemes.

MUDRA loans come in tiers: **Shishu** up to ₹50,000, **Kishor** ₹50,000-5 lakh and **Tarun** ₹5-10 lakh. **Tarun Plus** goes up to ₹20 lakh since October 2024.

### Farmers and villages
- **PM-KISAN** (February 2019): **₹6,000 a year** to landholding farmer families, in three direct transfers. The Agriculture Ministry runs it.
- **PM Fasal Bima Yojana** (2016): low-cost crop insurance.
- **e-NAM** (2016): one online market linking mandis.
- **Kisan Credit Card** (1998): short-term crop loans.
- **PM-KUSUM**: solar pumps for farmers.

> **Example:** ₹6,000 in three equal parts is ₹2,000 per instalment.

### Health, water, housing and fuel
| Scheme | Launch | Key fact |

| Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY | 23 Sep 2018 | ₹5 lakh cover per family a year for hospital care |
| Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission | Sep 2021 | Digital health stack; ABHA health ID |
| Jal Jeevan Mission | Aug 2019 | "Har Ghar Jal": tap water to every home |
| Swachh Bharat Mission | 2 Oct 2014 | Toilets; open-defecation-free goal |
| POSHAN Abhiyaan | 2018 | Nutrition, under the WCD Ministry |
| PM Awas Yojana | 2015 urban, 2016 rural | Pucca houses |
| PM Ujjwala Yojana | 1 May 2016 | Free LPG connections to poor women |
| Beti Bachao Beti Padhao | 2015 | Girl child; launched at Panipat |

Since 2024, **Vay Vandana** extends PM-JAY to everyone aged 70 and above.

### Industry, skills and energy
- **Make in India** (25 September 2014): manufacturing push.
- **Skill India / PMKVY** (2015): job skills.
- **Startup India** (16 January 2016): DPIIT recognition and tax holidays for startups.
- **UDAN** (2016): regional air links.
- **PLI schemes** (2020): production-linked incentives in 14 sectors.
- **PM Gati Shakti** (October 2021): national infrastructure master plan.
- **PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli** (2024): rooftop solar, up to 300 free units a month.

### Which ministry runs it
| Ministry | Schemes |

| Housing and Urban Affairs | PMAY-Urban, DAY-NULM, PM SVANidhi |
| Rural Development | MGNREGA line, DAY-NRLM |

### New in Budget 2026-27
The Budget of 1 February 2026 added these:
- **Biopharma SHAKTI**: ₹10,000 crore.
- **SME Growth Fund**: ₹10,000 crore.

subtopics.notes:
### Financial regulators
Each regulator watches one market. Learn the market, the year and the HQ together.

| Regulator | Watches | Set up | HQ |
|---|---|---|---|
| RBI | Banks, NBFCs, payments | 1935; nationalised 1949 | Mumbai |
| SEBI | Securities market | 1988; SEBI Act 1992 | Mumbai |
| IRDAI | Insurance | IRDA Act 1999 | Hyderabad |
| PFRDA | Pensions (NPS, APY) | Interim 2003; PFRDA Act 2013 | New Delhi |

SEBI became a statutory body after the Harshad Mehta episode. **RERA** (2016) regulates real estate.

The RBI Governor is **Sanjay Malhotra**. The SEBI chief is **Tuhin Kanta Pandey**, since March 2025.

> **Tip:** Stockbroker or mutual fund means SEBI. Policyholder means IRDAI. NPS means PFRDA.

### Development finance institutions
These banks lend to other lenders. This is called refinance.

- **NABARD** (**12 July 1982**): apex bank for rural credit. It came on the Shivaraman Committee's advice. It took over the RBI's farm refinance work. It refinances RRBs and co-operative banks. HQ Mumbai. The Government of India owns it.
- **SIDBI** (1990): refinance for small industries (MSMEs). HQ **Lucknow**. It is also the fund manager for MUDRA.
- **EXIM Bank** (1982): trade finance. HQ Mumbai.
- **NHB** (1988): housing finance. HQ New Delhi.

> **Watch:** Lucknow (SIDBI) and Hyderabad (IRDAI) are the two surprise HQs. Most others are in Mumbai.

### Stock exchanges and indices
The **BSE** (1875) is **Asia's oldest stock exchange**. It began as the Native Share and Stock Brokers' Association. Its index is the **Sensex, with 30 stocks**.

The **NSE** was set up in 1992 and began trading in 1994. It brought screen-based trading. Its index is the **Nifty 50**.

Both indices are free-float market-cap weighted. Shares are held in electronic form by two depositories, **NSDL and CDSL**.

### Payments and coordination
- **NPCI** (2008) runs India's retail payment rails: **UPI** (2016), RuPay, IMPS, FASTag and NACH.
- **FSDC** (Financial Stability and Development Council, 2010) coordinates all regulators. The Union Finance Minister chairs it.

### Bretton Woods and trade bodies
The IMF and the World Bank were both born at the **Bretton Woods conference in 1944**. Both sit in **Washington DC**.

| Body | Year | HQ | Role and head |
|---|---|---|---|
| IMF | 1944 | Washington DC | Balance-of-payments help, quotas, SDRs; MD Kristalina Georgieva |
| World Bank | 1944 (IBRD 1945) | Washington DC | IBRD + IDA, long-term loans; President Ajay Banga (since June 2023) |
| WTO | 1995 | Geneva | Trade rules; replaced GATT (1947); DG Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala |
| OECD | 1961 | Paris | India is not a member |
| FATF | 1989 | Paris | Money-laundering watchdog; India a member since 2010 |

IMF reports: World Economic Outlook and Global Financial Stability Report. The World Bank publishes the World Development Report. India is a founding member of the WTO.

### Asian and BRICS banks
| Bank | Year | HQ | Key fact |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADB | 1966 | Manila | President Masato Kanda (2025) |
| AIIB | 2016 | Beijing | India is the second-largest shareholder |
| NDB (BRICS bank) | 2015 | Shanghai | First president K.V. Kamath |

India is a founding member of all three.

> **Example:** "BRICS bank" in a question means NDB. Its HQ is Shanghai, not Beijing.
